---
title: "How did the Brexit uncertainty impact services exports of UK firms?"
description: >-
  **Journal of International Business Policy, 2025.** With Jun Du and Xiaocan Yuan.
  <details class="abstract-toggle"><summary onclick="event.preventDefault();
  event.stopPropagation(); this.closest('details').open =
  !this.closest('details').open;">Show abstract</summary>
  Using firm-level data and a synthetic difference-in-differences design, we
  estimate that Brexit-related policy uncertainty reduced UK services exports
  by 9.2% a year on average, a cumulative loss of roughly USD 146.8 billion
  between 2016 and 2019 — distinct from, and larger than, the effect of the
  tariff and non-tariff barriers that eventually took effect. The impact fell
  disproportionately on small and medium-sized exporters, while multinational
  enterprises were more likely to relocate operations outside the UK
  altogether.
  </details>
date: "2025-03-01"
status: "published"
categories: [brexit, firms, services-trade, firm-level]
doi: "10.1057/s42214-024-00202-6"
---

Brexit-related uncertainty had a measurable, negative effect on UK firms'
services exports — distinct from, and in some respects larger than, the
effect of the tariff and non-tariff barriers that eventually took effect.
Using firm-level export data and a synthetic difference-in-differences
design, we isolate the uncertainty channel from the trade-policy channel by
comparing UK firms to a synthetic control built from firms in countries
that faced no comparable shock.

**Published in:** *Journal of International Business Policy*, 8(1), 80–104
